paths.title: Accessibility & Internationalization
paths.description: Ensure generated products work for diverse users, input methods, languages, locales, and content lengths.

lessons.title: Use semantic structure
lessons.principle: Assistive technology depends on meaningful markup.
lessons.practice: Use headings, landmarks, lists, tables, labels, and native controls according to purpose.

lessons.title: Provide accessible names
lessons.principle: Icon-only controls are ambiguous without text alternatives.
lessons.practice: Ensure interactive elements have meaningful visible labels or accessible names.

lessons.title: Maintain visible focus
lessons.principle: Keyboard users need to know where interaction is occurring.
lessons.practice: Use clear focus indicators with adequate contrast and never remove focus without replacement.

lessons.title: Support complete keyboard operation
lessons.principle: Every pointer interaction should have a keyboard path.
lessons.practice: Test tab order, activation, escape, arrow-key patterns, and no keyboard traps.

lessons.title: Manage dialog focus
lessons.principle: Modal interfaces require predictable focus containment and restoration.
lessons.practice: Move focus into dialogs, trap appropriately, and restore to the invoking control on close.

lessons.title: Announce dynamic updates
lessons.principle: Screen-reader users may not notice visual state changes.
lessons.practice: Use appropriate live regions or status semantics for important asynchronous feedback.

lessons.title: Meet contrast requirements
lessons.principle: Muted AI-generated palettes can become unreadable.
lessons.practice: Measure text, icon, control, and focus contrast instead of judging by appearance.

lessons.title: Support zoom and text resizing
lessons.principle: Fixed layouts can break when users enlarge content.
lessons.practice: Allow reflow and avoid clipping at high zoom or larger text settings.

lessons.title: Respect motion preferences
lessons.principle: Animation can cause discomfort or distract from tasks.
lessons.practice: Reduce or remove nonessential motion when the user requests reduced motion.

lessons.title: Provide text alternatives
lessons.principle: Images and charts need equivalent meaning.
lessons.practice: Write concise alt text or nearby descriptions based on the image's purpose.

lessons.title: Use accessible form errors
lessons.principle: Color alone is not a sufficient error signal.
lessons.practice: Associate clear error text with the relevant field and focus or summarize errors appropriately.

lessons.title: Test with assistive technology
lessons.principle: Automated scanners do not cover all usability.
lessons.practice: Perform keyboard and representative screen-reader testing on critical flows.

lessons.title: Externalize user-facing strings
lessons.principle: Hard-coded strings block translation workflows.
lessons.practice: Keep translatable content separate from code and avoid string concatenation that assumes word order.

lessons.title: Design for text expansion
lessons.principle: Translations can be substantially longer than source text.
lessons.practice: Use flexible layouts and test long labels, buttons, and navigation.

lessons.title: Use locale-aware formatting
lessons.principle: Dates, numbers, currencies, and plural rules differ by locale.
lessons.practice: Use internationalization APIs and explicit locale or time-zone handling.

lessons.title: Avoid encoding meaning in color only
lessons.principle: Color perception varies and assistive technology may not convey color.
lessons.practice: Combine color with text, icons, patterns, or position.

lessons.title: Support right-to-left layout when required
lessons.principle: RTL languages affect alignment, order, and directional icons.
lessons.practice: Use logical CSS properties and test mirrored layouts.

lessons.title: Localize validation thoughtfully
lessons.principle: Input formats and names vary across cultures.
lessons.practice: Avoid assumptions about postal codes, names, phone numbers, and date entry beyond business requirements.

lessons.title: Include accessibility in acceptance criteria
lessons.principle: Accessibility work is missed when treated as optional polish.
lessons.practice: Specify keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast, and announcements in the feature definition.

lessons.title: Prevent regression with automation
lessons.principle: Accessibility needs continuous protection.
lessons.practice: Add linting and automated checks while retaining manual verification for critical interactions.

paths.title: Development Environments, Docker & Reproducibility
paths.description: Make AI-assisted changes reproducible across machines through explicit environments, containers, configuration, and setup automation.

lessons.title: Make setup deterministic
lessons.principle: Agents and humans need the same prerequisites.
lessons.practice: Document runtime versions, package manager, system dependencies, and startup commands.

lessons.title: Pin toolchain versions
lessons.principle: Unbounded runtime upgrades can change behavior unexpectedly.
lessons.practice: Use version files, lockfiles, container tags or digests, and reproducible package installation.

lessons.title: Use environment templates
lessons.principle: Developers need configuration shape without real secrets.
lessons.practice: Commit a safe example environment file documenting required variables and defaults.

lessons.title: Separate secrets from config
lessons.principle: Configuration may be versioned; credentials should not be.
lessons.practice: Inject secrets through protected environment or secret-management systems.

lessons.title: Use containers when isolation helps
lessons.principle: Containers can standardize dependencies and services across hosts.
lessons.practice: Containerize development components where reproducibility outweighs local complexity.

lessons.title: Keep images small and deterministic
lessons.principle: Huge mutable images slow builds and obscure provenance.
lessons.practice: Use specific bases, multi-stage builds, minimal runtime layers, and clean build contexts.

lessons.title: Use Docker Compose for local stacks
lessons.principle: Multi-service development benefits from one declarative topology.
lessons.practice: Define services, networks, volumes, health checks, and safe development overrides in Compose.

lessons.title: Wait for readiness, not process start
lessons.principle: A running dependency may still be initializing.
lessons.practice: Use health checks and retry-aware clients instead of fixed sleeps.

lessons.title: Persist only intended data
lessons.principle: Container filesystems are ephemeral by design.
lessons.practice: Use named volumes or bind mounts deliberately and know what survives recreation.

lessons.title: Avoid mounting secrets casually
lessons.principle: Host mounts and environment values can broaden exposure.
lessons.practice: Use supported secret mechanisms and minimize what containers can read.

lessons.title: Use development watch carefully
lessons.principle: Live synchronization improves iteration but changes runtime behavior.
lessons.practice: Define what is synced, ignored, rebuilt, or restarted and keep production images immutable.

lessons.title: Match CI and local commands
lessons.principle: Different validation paths create works-on-my-machine failures.
lessons.practice: Run the same scripts and tool versions locally and in continuous integration.

lessons.title: Provide one-command bootstrap
lessons.principle: Setup friction wastes agent and developer cycles.
lessons.practice: Automate dependency installation, local services, migrations, and seed data safely.

lessons.title: Make seeds idempotent
lessons.principle: Repeated setup should not corrupt local state.
lessons.practice: Design development seed scripts that can rerun or reset predictably.

lessons.title: Handle platform differences
lessons.principle: Filesystem case, line endings, architecture, and shell behavior can vary.
lessons.practice: Test or containerize assumptions that matter across macOS, Windows, Linux, and ARM/x86.

lessons.title: Keep dev and production concerns separate
lessons.principle: Development convenience settings can be insecure or slow in production.
lessons.practice: Use explicit production configuration and do not rely on hot reload, source mounts, or debug flags.

lessons.title: Document reset and recovery
lessons.principle: Local environments inevitably drift.
lessons.practice: Provide commands to clear caches, recreate containers, reset data, and reinstall dependencies.

lessons.title: Cache builds safely
lessons.principle: Caching accelerates iteration but can hide stale inputs.
lessons.practice: Key caches to lockfiles and build inputs and provide clean-build paths.

lessons.title: Verify offline or degraded development where relevant
lessons.principle: Cloud-only tooling can block work during outages.
lessons.practice: Identify which dependencies are mandatory online and provide local substitutes where valuable.

lessons.title: Treat environment code as product code
lessons.principle: Container and setup files control execution and security.
lessons.practice: Review Dockerfiles, Compose, scripts, and devcontainer configuration with normal code-review rigor.

codeExamples.snippet:
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

services:
  app:
    build: .
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:17
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
